output:
## UX review: skill pages a11y-audit, copy-tight and spec-writer Reviewed: the header and first section of three skill pages built from one template (code only). Layout input: none. Main goal: install the skill shown on the page Steps to main goal: 1 (press the copy-install-command button) Findings: 2 (S1: 0, S2: 1, S3: 1, S4: 0) ### Findings 1. **Header template on 3 pages: a11y-audit, copy-tight, spec-writer; header "Install" link** | S2 Major | R-ux-review-11 - Evidence: "Install" - User experiences: The user clicks Install in the header, expecting this skill's install, and is taken off the page to the collection index. - Recommendation: Make the header Install link lead to this page's own install section, or give it a label that does not suggest installing this skill. 2. **spec-writer page, "Compare" section** | S3 Minor | R-ux-review-30 - Evidence: "

Compare

" - User experiences: The user sees two equally prominent install buttons, one under Install and one under Compare, and wonders whether they differ. - Recommendation: Keep one primary install action on the page and show any repeat in the Compare section as a secondary control. ### Not reviewed - Contrast, focus styles, spacing and type scales: a visual polish pass. - Semantics, ARIA and screen-reader output: an accessibility audit. - Wording of labels and messages: a copy edit. ### Open questions - "Copy install command" button on all three pages: the input does not show whether a visible confirmation follows the copy, or whether the command is displayed. - Collection page "#install" section: the input does not show what it contains. - Layout of all three pages: page height, first-screen order and the position of the install section are not given. ### Severity scale - S1 Blocker: the user cannot complete the main goal, or loses data or money. - S2 Major: the user completes the main goal only after a wrong action, an error or a second attempt. - S3 Minor: the user completes the main goal at the first attempt, but more slowly. - S4 Note: the result and the speed do not change; the place departs from the rule.
